editorial:
Imagine you are a brave soldier who gets told by three creepy witches that you will one day be the king. That is exactly what happens to Macbeth, and it starts a wild ride of greed and betrayal. Along with his wife, who is even more driven than he is, Macbeth decides to take a shortcut to the top by killing the current king. The whole movie feels like a dark dream, with a lot of gray colors and strange sets that make you feel like you are trapped in a nightmare. It is a story about how wanting too much power can totally ruin your life.

Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand are amazing in this, and they make the old-school talking feel natural and easy to follow. The black and white look is a huge plus because it makes every scene look like a piece of art. While it moves a bit slow at times, the tension keeps you glued to the screen. If you have a high-end TV, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Apple TV to see all the detail, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection. It is a great pick for a rainy night.
endingExplained: In the end, Macbeth realizes the witches tricked him with their riddles. He thought he was safe until a forest moved toward his castle, but it was actually just soldiers hiding behind tree branches. Macduff, the man who fights him, reveals he was not born the normal way, which breaks the spell of protection. Macduff kills Macbeth in a sword fight, and the rightful prince takes back the throne to bring peace to Scotland.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strong acting and dark stories about power.
